label: conj:three-calibration-inputs
title: Exactly three calibration inputs: every observable factors through $m_e$, $m_\pi$ and $q_0$
html:
Beyond the three calibration inputs, no further empirical, fitting, or numerological input is needed: every other mass, Q-value, binding energy, coupling constant, mixing angle, and dimensionless ratio in the paper is a prediction. Precisely, it is conjectured that for every canonical observable \mathcal{O} in the paper — mass \mathfrak{m}, Q-value \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, binding B(Z, N), crossing energy E_{\mathfrak{H}}, coupling \alpha, mixing angle, shell parameter — there exists a \mathbb{Q}(q_0)-element \hat{\mathcal{O}}(q_0) \in \mathbb{Z}[q_0^{\pm 1/2}] and integers a, b \in \mathbb{Z} with

  \mathcal{O}
  \;=\;
  \hat{\mathcal{O}}(q_0)
  \cdot
  m_e^{\,a}
  \cdot
  m_\pi^{\,b}

with a + b \in \{0, 1\} (dimensionless, mass-scale, or energy-scale output) and q_0 fixed by CAL-2 (P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}, pinned canonical through its proxy m_\mu/m_e). The two dimensional bridges to MeV are the proxy scales m_e and m_\pi; the derived hadronic energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0 = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) and the CAL-2 proxy \mathfrak{Q}_\beta are m_e^{1}\cdot\mathbb{Q}(q_0) expressions, not independent factors.

The three calibration observables, the allowed and forbidden substitutions, the (co)homological alignment, and the comparison with the Standard Model are collected in the calibration-discipline context.
heading: Conjecture
